Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

efficient adjective

getting things done without waste

also efficiently, efficiency, businesslike

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.3.53: homō gnāvus et industrius (Lewis & Short)

nāvus (gnāvus), nāva, nāvum

adjective · Wiktionary

brisk, businesslike, active (of a person)

Of people who get on with the work: busy, diligent, active (Lewis & Short). Its noun nāvitās and adverb nāviter follow.

Other words

  • compendiārius, compendiāria, compendiārium — short, quick (of a way or method)

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.43: via ad glōriam proxima et quasi compendiāria (Lewis & Short); Sen. Ep. 119.1 · Declension on Wiktionary

    From compendium, a saving; compendiāria (sc. via) is a short cut. Rare: Cicero has it once.

  • habilis, habile — handy, manageable; skilful

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 308; Cic. de Or. 1.231 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Traupman’s word for efficient. Classically of what is easy to handle (shoes, a sword) and of a person apt or nimble; habilitās is aptitude.

  • efficiēns, efficientis — efficient

    adjective, third declension · also used · modern · Traupman 152; Cic. Top. 14 fin. (Lewis & Short, s.v. efficiō) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically “bringing about, producing”, the philosophers’ causa efficiēns; the sense “efficient” is Traupman’s. Cicero’s adverb efficienter (Fat. 34) is causal too.

  • habilitās, habilitātis f. — aptitude (Traupman: efficiency)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 1.27: opportūnitātēs habilitātēsque reliquī corporis (Lewis & Short); Traupman 308 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically aptitude, fitness of the body; Traupman uses it for efficiency.

Examples

  • homō gnāvus et industrius

    a brisk and hard-working manCic. Verr. 2.3.53 (Lewis & Short)

  • Gnāvus est; plūs ūnā hōrā cōnficit quam aliī tōtō diē.

    He’s efficient; he gets more done in an hour than others in a whole day.composed

See also effective, active.
